newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr buying by Japan pension funds expected - traders.
newsitem.headline: Dlr buying by Japan pension funds expected - traders.

text.p: Japanese pension funds are expected to buy several hundred billion yen worth of dollars through trust banks this month, banking sources said on Wednesday.
The sources said about 300 billion yen in pension money was likely to be invested via trust banks in foreign assets, such as stocks and bonds, by the middle of this month.
Trust bank sources said although the exact amount remained unknown, a larger share of the dollar purchases would be made through foreign trust banks in Japan than through Japanese trust banks.

Separately, there was also speculation that public fund bodies, such as the Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo), may invest in foreign assets, using some of the money earned from the redemption of Japanese government bonds, dealers said.
About five trillion yen worth of Japanese government bonds with coupon rates of 4-5 percent will mature on June 20.
Kampo is a major institutional investor which holds its securities until they mature.

A Kampo official declined to comment on whether it will switch some of the maturing funds to overseas assets, but agreed that the dollar/yen exchange rate had become more stable after its wild swings in May.
Market sources said Kampo has been relatively quiet after increasing its dollar purchases in February.
Currency traders said expectations of dollar purchases by the trust banks and public fund bodies could become a dollar-supportive factor.
